rounds.text: Getalong Enterprise Ltd presents an alarming trajectory of structural revenue collapse, highlighted by a compounded sales growth of -59% over five years and a severe -64% contraction over the trailing twelve months [E14, E16]. This top-line deterioration is further underscored by a recent TTM profit growth decline of -62%, signaling that the brief three-year profit recovery has completely unraveled [E17, E18, E19]. Compounding these fundamental business risks, the stock trades at an expensive P/E of 37.48x against a sector benchmark of 20.32x, while also carrying a premium P/B of 2.23x compared to its sector benchmark of 1.54x [E6, E7]. Furthermore, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00%, failing to reward shareholders for holding these heightened operational risks [E4]. Market expectations have detached from reality as price growth recently exceeds profit growth by 20%, leaving the company vulnerable to severe valuation corrections as declining sales catch up to the share price [E51]. Conceded: [E8].

The bear exaggerates structural collapse by ignoring the clear multi-year profit turnaround where compounded profit growth stands at 23% over three years [E18], supported by positive screen signals for year-over-year profit growth exceeding 20% and rising quarter-over-quarter sales [E63, E65]. The operational efficiency of the business is superior to the bear's gloomy portrayal, evidenced by a strong return on assets of 2.78% that outperforms the sector benchmark of 1.37% [E8]. While the bear points to high relative valuation multiples from data providers [E6, E7], filed statements show a much more moderate trailing P/E of 24.3 and an attractive price-to-book ratio of just 1.06x on a book value of ₹ 7.27 against a share price of ₹ 7.70 [E1, E2]. Furthermore, the stock trades at only 48% of its 52-week range, indicating that current market capitalisation of ₹ 16.3 Cr has plenty of room to appreciate before hitting historical highs [E3, E5]. Conceded: [E4, E14, E16].

The bull relies heavily on a three-year profit turnaround of 23% [E18] and positive screens [E63, E65], yet glosses over a severe collapse in the trailing twelve months where compounded sales growth plummeted by -64% and profit growth cratered by -62% [E16, E19]. While the bull cites a strong return on assets of 2.78% versus the sector benchmark of 1.37% [E8], this efficiency metric is overshadowed by a multi-year structural decay where compounded sales growth over five years sits at a disastrous -59% [E14, E57]. The bull's attempt to downplay valuation by using filed statements for a 24.3 P/E [E1] ignores alternative provider data showing an inflated P/E of 37.48x against a sector benchmark of 20.32x [E6], meaning expectations are already running ahead of delivery as price growth exceeds profit growth by 20% [E51]. Conceded: [E2, E3, E4, E5, E7, E15, E17, E73, E74].
